correctness.rationale: The positive inverse of sI+fL times A is strictly positive. The positive radial eigenvector therefore certifies the full Perron root. In the coordinates (hub, representative leaf), the radial kernel has common diagonal mf and off-diagonals m(s+f), s+mf, times ξf/((1+f)s(s+(m+1)f)), giving the stated formula. The decreasing variable r=sqrt(m(s+f)/(s+mf)) maps positive f onto (1,sqrt(m)); the derivative with respect to r has the sign of s−S_m(r). All three terms of (log S_m)' are positive, so S_m runs from s_c to infinity and equality s=s_c gives strict increase at every finite f. The endpoint limits and m=1 specialization follow directly. Positivity of K makes the derivative of the left-Perron linear functional strictly negative off zero even at equality on the forward-invariant cube. Above threshold, the positive right Perron vector times a small scalar is a strict subsolution; monotone iteration under the all-ones supersolution gives a positive equilibrium. For the witness, r=2 gives f=5 and Λ=1/9. A separate exact bracket check uses the sign of 1/10−Λ(f), equal to the sign of f³−42f²+57f+20: the positive quantity 18f²+74f+40 is compared to 4f sqrt((20+f)(20+16f)), and the difference of squares factors as 4(17f+20) times that cubic. The signs at 1, 7/4, 40, 42 are respectively the signs of 36, −225/64, −900, 2414; bisection matches both stated roots.
residual_risks: The frozen RESULT describes its bundled crossing comparisons as exact fraction/radical checks; check.py uses floating-point sqrt and comparisons there. The exact cubic check above independently supplies the needed certificate.
